newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.400 cent per lb lower to 0.500 higher while feeder cattle futures were called steady to 0.300 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Carryover sell stops from Wednesday's limit down close are likely, but analysts expect live cattle futures to quickly turn higher on what is considered an over-reaction to the rumor of an Indiana rose farmer dying from Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), a human illness similar to bovine spongiform encphalopathy (BSE). There is no evidence to point to any connection with the U.S. cattle herd which is BSE free, several traders said.

They noted that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration late Wednesday said they do not believe there is any link from using bone meal fertilizer and BSE, sometimes called "mad cow disease". The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said deaths in the U.S. from CJD were rare and not known to be linked to "mad cow" disease.
However, the recovery in live cattle may be limited by weak technicals after the break and Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report, analysts said.

Estimates for cattle on feed in seven-state major feedlots averaged 107.6 percent of a year ago and ranged from 106 to 108 percent of last year. March placement estimates averaged 103.3 percent of a year ago and ranged from 100.5 to 107 percent and marketings estimates averaged 100.6 percent and ranged from 98 to 104.5 percent.
Feeder cattle futures were also expected to rebound after following live cattle futures lower Wednesday. The market was oversold on spillover pressure, traders said.
They also anticipated support from recent firm demand for replacement feeders, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.06 at $70.59 per cwt.
